candidates.rationale: Every metric here is near-best (stability 1.00, low turnover cost, moderate half-life) except one: nearest-archive rho is 0.792, the tightest margin to the 0.80 cap in the batch, against sibling c33fa1e63a674a2d. The shared driver is the symmetric 21-day high/low range. Widening only the ceiling window to 42 decouples that range definition while leaving the reactive floor and close anchor untouched.

The one real flaw is a regime break: IC fades from about +0.02 in the mid-2000s to -0.0023 in 2013, the only sign-losing year in the set (stability 0.93). The 10-day volatility denominator is the most regime-sensitive piece, since short realized-vol windows get noisy exactly when a low-vol grind-up regime sets in. Lengthening it to 21 days stabilizes the normalizer.

Nothing is broken operationally (stability 1.00, low turnover cost); the weak number is archive proximity, rho 0.780 against sibling 0168481b31dce7bc, second tightest margin in the batch. Both share an identical TS_MEAN($return, 10) node. Shortening it to 5 days breaks the piece most likely driving that correlation.

Only 2012 breaks an otherwise clean sign record (stability 0.93), a regime blip more plausibly sourced in the short 10-day return-mean leg than the earnings-yield leg, since short-horizon momentum terms are the classic regime-flippers. Lengthening that window to 21 days smooths it and further separates this factor from sibling 693246746bbdc073's shared node.

candidates.changed_node: outer / -> *, with the now-unneeded + 1e-8 guard removed
candidates.rationale: Stability is 0.93 with only 2013 negative, but working memory already flags this exact family: plain ratios of a range term over a dollar-volume rank are archive-saturated, while rank-product and rank-difference versions of the same pieces are the shapes that keep clearing. Swapping the ratio for a product, and dropping the epsilon it no longer needs, is the direct fix.

Turnover and half-life are both excellent; the odd piece is mixing a bounded CS_RANK leg with an unbounded CS_ZSCORE leg, a scale mismatch that leaves the difference exposed to outlier-driven volume spikes, a plausible source of the 2003 sign flip. Matching both legs to CS_RANK aligns this with the rank-difference shape already validated for this fundamental/volume pairing.

candidates.changed_node: TS_MEAN($return, 63) -> TS_MEAN($return, 21), the COUNT baseline window
candidates.rationale: This is the textbook case named in the brief: positive IC in 12 years, negative in exactly two (2009, 2012), both sharp trend-regime transitions. A 5-day count against a 63-day baseline is maximally exposed to that mismatch, since a sustained trend drags the long baseline and saturates the count. Shrinking the baseline to 21 days narrows the mismatch.

Two consecutive negative years, 2009 and 2010, sit right on the crisis volume spike-and-decay period. The 21-day dollar-volume smoothing is short enough to still be distorted by that transient spike. Lengthening it to 63 days makes the liquidity term closer to a stable size proxy.

candidates.changed_node: outer TS_RANK(..., 63) -> TS_RANK(..., 10), the percentile window
candidates.rationale: Half-life is 3.8 days, the shortest in the batch by a wide margin, meaning the effect is very short-lived. Feeding that from a 63-day trailing volume-percentile window means most of the percentile's information is stale relative to the horizon it predicts. Shortening that outer window to 10 days matches construction horizon to the observed decay speed.

Turnover is 0.314 one-way, the highest in the batch, charging 0.011 of fitness, a cost this factor is not clearly earning back. The likely source is ranking raw, unsmoothed $dollar_volume, far noisier day to day than the smoothed version used in the much lower-turnover sibling 60d56d6cb6783cd9. Inserting a 5-day mean before the TS_RANK should reduce that churn.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Plain ratio-of-two-raw-terms variants in the spread/dollar-volume family are archive-saturated; the rank-product and rank-difference shapes are not.
  4. A crossover call failed outright this round from exceeding the output token cap, losing that paid call for nothing. Bias crossover toward smaller/shallower parent-tree pairs so the combined output stays in budget.
  5. archive_subtree's frozen threshold is 4 nodes, so any exact fragment that size or larger is burned permanently even when it's only half of an otherwise new expression.
